- Paragraph 47 mentions that Craig McFadzean, Plaintiff Turn8's representative, admitted he did not rely on anything specific in the Impugned Documents for investment decisions (Page 5)
- Paragraph 50 denies any fault in violation of Article 1457 of the CCQ and asserts no loss was suffered by Plaintiffs or other Class Members (Page 5)
- TD Bank's statements about legendary, outstanding, and efficient customer service were confirmed by third-party industry awards (Page 6)
- TD Canada Trust was ranked "highest in customer satisfaction" among big five retail banks in 2015 for the tenth year in a row (Page 6)
- The 2015 J.D. Power Canadian Retail Banking Customer Satisfaction Study surveyed over 14,000 customers in April and May 2015 (Page 6)
- TD Canada Trust ranked first in Customer Service Excellence in 2016 for the twelfth year in a row based on the Ipsos Best Banking Awards (Page 6)
- The 2016 Best Banking Awards survey had a sample size of 47,305 completed surveys as of August 2016 (Page 6)
- TD Canada Trust was voted the Most Trusted Brand in 2016 for the fifth year in a row according to the Reader's Digest survey (Page 6)
- TD Bank was recognized as one of Canada's Best Employers for 2017 for the eighth consecutive year (Page 7)
- TD Bank has been consistently recognized by The Great Place to Work Institute since 2006 (Page 7)
- TD Bank has been acknowledged as one of MediaCorp's Top 100 Employers in Canada annually since 2008 (Page 7)
- The 2015 and 2016 Outlook and Key Priorities sections of the MD&As were not unequivocal guarantees of future conduct (Page 7)
- TD Bank created a Fair and Responsible Banking Compliance Group to oversee unethical practices (Page 7)
- The bank's risk management embodies a tone at the top set by management, accepting only understandable risks (Page 7)
- Paragraph 60 states that TD Bank's disclosure of its definition of reputational risks was neither false nor misleading (Page 8)
- Paragraph 61 notes that statements from TD Bank's Code of Conduct and Ethics were not deliberately or unintentionally false or misleading (Page 8)
- Paragraph 62 highlights that the Plaintiffs have failed to prove a "Pressure Selling Program" and based their claim on analogies to the Wells Fargo scandal (Page 8)
- Paragraph 63 criticizes the reliance on hearsay allegations in the CBC Reports, which are described as vague, unverifiable, unsubstantiated, and subjective (Page 8)
- Paragraph 64 points out that the CBC Reports fail to identify employees who were fired or threatened and lack evidence of unrealistic incentive targets or policies (Page 8)
- Paragraph 65 states that the Plaintiffs have not provided an iota of evidence confirming TD Bank's failure to monitor reputational risk matters or that its internal controls were defective (Page 8)
- Paragraph 66 mentions that conclusions cannot be reasonably inferred from isolated, unidentifiable, and unverifiable recriminations involving about 100 million customer interactions and more than 81,000 employees annually (Page 8)
- Paragraph 67 asserts that all impugned statements fail to qualify as misrepresentations because they fall short of the applicable statutory materiality standard (Page 8)
- Paragraph 68 discusses the Plaintiffs' allegation that TD Bank's reported Canadian retail revenue increases were misleading due to omitted mis-selling programs (Page 9)
- Paragraph 69 states that materiality is an essential condition for statutory misrepresentation and cannot be triggered without a finding of materiality (Page 9)
- Paragraph 70 explains that materiality involves a case-by-case application of a legal standard to a factual matrix (Page 9)
- Paragraph 71 notes the burden to establish materiality rests with the Plaintiffs and cannot be presumed (Page 9)
- Paragraph 72 identifies the Plaintiffs' failure to meet this burden, citing their reliance on the wrong standard (reasonable investor test) (Page 9)
- Paragraph 73 clarifies that the QSA's approach to materiality is based on a narrower market impact test, not the reasonable investor test (Page 9)
- Paragraph 74 confirms that both material fact and changes are subject to an objective market impact test under Sections 5 and 5.3 of the QSA (Page 9)
- Paragraph 75 criticizes the Plaintiffs' allegation as grammatically incongruent and predicated on a purported expert report (Exhibit P-24) that relies on the incorrect reasonable investor test (Page 9)
- Paragraph 76 reiterates that the statutory definition of materiality depends on whether the misrepresentations could objectively have had a significant effect on market price or value (Page 9)
- Paragraph 77 defines the market impact test as being based on strictly economic terms and limiting actionable misrepresentations to those impacting the objective interest of all investors in financial return (Page 9)
- Paragraph 78 states that the Plaintiffs are aware that TD Bank's financial statements were never restated and no sanctions were asserted against the Bank or its directors and officers related to the CBC Reports (Page 9)
- Isolated concerns about mis-selling cannot significantly impact TD Bank's stock price due to its size (Page 10)
- TD Bank has over 81,000 employees, 1,165 branches, and 15 million customers in Canada (Page 10)
- The FCAC was established in 2001 by the Government of Canada to monitor compliance with consumer protection legislation (Page 10)
- The FCAC investigated six leading banks and concluded there was no evidence of systemic or widespread mis-selling (Page 10)
- The FCAC reviewed 4,500 complaints, 100,000 pages of documentation, and conducted 600 interviews with bank personnel (Page 10)
- Courts have confirmed that class actions are not commissions of inquiry and should not be used to overturn industry regulator findings (Page 10)
- Plaintiff Turn8 purchased TD Bank shares on February 14, 2018, at $72.32 following the CBC Reports (Page 11)
- The CBC Reports did not amount to admissible evidence or a legal basis for a QSA claim (Page 11)
- The March 6, 2017 CBC Report did not unleash a "firestorm" but only speculation (Page 11)
- The March 10, 2017 CBC Report was an unverifiable complement to previously disclosed mis-selling allegations (Page 11)
- The TD Bank stock price increased after the March 6 report and dropped after the March 10 report, indicating markets were responding to stoked fears (Page 11)
- The March 2017 CBC Reports were posted on the heels of the 2016 Wells Fargo systemic mis-selling scandal, as referenced in Exhibit D-3 (Page 11)
- The Wells Fargo scandal involved 3.5 million unauthorized customer credit-card and bank accounts (Page 12)
- Wells Fargo was fined $US185 million on September 8, 2016, and paid $US2.7 billion in civil and criminal lawsuits (Page 12)
- TD Bank's stock drop following the March 10, 2017 CBC Report was attributed to speculative fears, not factual corrections (Page 12)
- Analyst reports from BMO, Eight Capital, and Credit Suisse confirmed the stock drop was due to fear and speculation (Page 12)
- The market's rush to judgment was understandable given the Wells Fargo scandal, but concluding TD's situation was the same is a stretch (Page 12)
- The March 20, 2018 FCAC report found no evidence of widespread mis-selling at TD Bank or five other largest Canadian banks (Page 13)
- The plaintiffs' claim about a CBC report interfering with the FCAC findings is described as "entirely false" (Page 13)
- No evidence of reliance on the Impugned Documents has been provided by the plaintiffs (Page 13)
- Class Members do not benefit from any statutory calculation facilitating their burden to establish a veritable loss under the CCQ (Page 13)
- An individual recovery scheme is necessary to preserve TD Bank's right to a full and unfettered defence (Page 13)
- Class Members residing outside of Québec cannot avail themselves of Québec law (Page 13)
